refined_descriptions.sql-explainer: Explains what an existing SQL query does, breaking down clauses, joins, subqueries, and execution order in plain language for review or learning. Unlike cron-scheduler, which writes and validates cron schedule expressions, this skill only interprets database queries and never deals with schedules or cron syntax. It does not write, optimize, debug, or rewrite SQL, does not execute queries against a database, and does not cover database design, administration, or performance tuning.
refined_descriptions.pdf-signature-check: Inspects PDF files to detect digital signatures and reports whether each signature is valid. Covers signature presence, validity status, and signer details where available. Differs from cron-scheduler, which writes and validates cron expressions from plain-language schedules; this skill handles only PDF signature checking, not scheduling or time-based tasks. Does not sign, add, or remove signatures, does not repair broken signatures, and does not verify passwords, encryption, or general PDF integrity.
refined_descriptions.email-drafter: Drafts reply text for customer support emails using the support tone guide. Unlike git-bisector, which runs git bisect to locate bug-introducing commits, this skill handles written customer communication and never inspects code history or repositories. It does not send, schedule, or deliver emails; it does not triage tickets, handle internal or non-customer mail, edit the tone guide, or perform any git or version-control operations.
refined_descriptions.csv-merger: Merges multiple CSV files into a single file by joining rows on a shared key column. Unlike csv-cleaner, which fixes quoting, whitespace, and column names within one file, this skill only combines files; it performs no cleaning or repair of malformed values, does not create or edit columns, and does not merge files lacking a common key column. Use it to combine datasets; use csv-cleaner for formatting fixes.
refined_descriptions.git-conflict-resolver: Explains Git merge conflicts hunk by hunk in a branch and suggests a resolution for each conflicting hunk based on both sides' changes. Handles version-control conflicts only, unlike cron-scheduler, which builds and validates cron schedule expressions from plain language. Does not write or validate cron expressions, schedule recurring jobs, rebase or cherry-pick commits, resolve binary-file conflicts, or automatically apply merges; it explains conflicts and proposes fixes only.
refined_descriptions.log-anomaly: Detects anomalies in already-parsed, structured log records: unusual patterns, rate spikes, and suspicious lines, returned with severity flags. Operates downstream of log-parser; unlike log-parser, it does not read, parse, or convert raw server logs, and it expects timestamped, leveled records as input. Does not remediate flagged issues, correlate logs with metrics or traces, send alerts through external systems, or store logs. Use log-parser first when input is raw log text.
refined_descriptions.api-diff: Compares two OpenAPI specification documents and reports breaking changes affecting API clients, such as removed endpoints, changed parameters, and altered response schemas. Works on structured specification files; unlike email-triage, it performs no classification of intent, urgency, or language and processes no inbound messages. Does not modify or merge specifications, does not generate client code, does not test running endpoints, and does not handle email or support inbox triage.
refined_descriptions.regex-explainer: Explains an existing regular expression by breaking it down token by token and describing what each part matches, in plain language. Operates only on regexes that are already provided; it decodes and clarifies them but does not create, modify, debug, optimize, or test regular expressions. Unlike regex-builder, which generates a regex from a plain-language description and test strings, this skill performs the reverse task: interpreting an expression back into words. Requests to build or refine a regex are out of scope.
refined_descriptions.cron-explainer: Explains existing cron expressions in plain language: each field's meaning, the resulting schedule, and quirks such as day-of-month/day-of-week OR behavior, steps, ranges, and nonstandard values. Works in the reverse direction from cron-scheduler, which generates and validates expressions from a described schedule; this skill only interprets expressions, never produces them. Does not write, edit, validate, or fix cron expressions, convert schedules into cron syntax, or execute, register, or manage scheduled jobs.
refined_descriptions.doc-translator: Translates document files or text between languages while preserving formatting, structure, and terminology. Differs from email-triage: that skill classifies inbound support email by intent, urgency, and language; this skill translates content and never classifies or routes messages. Excludes drafting or composing new documents, summarizing, tone rewriting, message classification, and live interpretation. Output is the source document rendered in the target language.
refined_descriptions.image-captioner: Generates short alt-text captions for image files using a vision model; accepts common image formats and returns a one-sentence description of the visual content. Unlike doc-summarizer, which condenses long text documents into abstracts, this skill takes images as input, not text, and produces a new caption rather than a shortened version of existing prose. Does not summarize text documents, extract or transcribe text within images (OCR), edit or generate images, or answer questions about image content.
refined_descriptions.slide-auditor: Inspects presentation slide decks and reports layout and accessibility issues: overflowing or clipped text, unreadable contrast between text and background, and slides missing speaker notes. Unlike cron-scheduler, which converts plain-language schedules into cron expressions, this skill works only with slide files and performs no scheduling or time-based tasks. It does not create, edit, restyle, or redesign slides, fix detected issues automatically, write missing speaker notes, or generate deck content; it only audits existing decks and reports findings.
refined_descriptions.sql-migrator: Translates SQL queries between database dialects (e.g., Oracle to PostgreSQL, SQL Server to Snowflake), rewriting syntax, functions, and data types to run on the target engine while preserving the query's logic. Differs from sql-optimizer, which speeds up slow queries using index hints, join ordering, and partition pruning: this skill changes only dialect, not performance. Excludes performance tuning, indexing or partitioning advice, and schema or data migration.
refined_descriptions.pdf-watermarker: Stamps text watermarks across pages of PDF files and reports which pages were changed. Differs from pdf-signature-check, which inspects PDF digital signatures for presence and validity without modifying files; this skill modifies PDF page content by adding watermarks and never examines signatures. Does not detect, validate, add, or remove digital signatures, does not apply image or logo watermarks, does not remove existing watermarks, and does not verify passwords, encryption, or general PDF integrity.
refined_descriptions.email-digest: Summarizes email threads and message chains into short bullet digests with extracted action items, owners, and deadlines. Unlike doc-summarizer, which handles general text documents such as articles and reports, this skill processes only email conversations and preserves reply structure and thread context. Does not summarize standalone documents, PDFs, articles, attachments, or non-email text, and does not draft or send email replies; use doc-summarizer for general document abstracts.
refined_descriptions.csv-deduper: Detects duplicate rows in CSV files and reports which columns matched for each duplicate found. Unlike csv-cleaner, which fixes quoting, strips whitespace, and normalizes column names, this skill performs no formatting cleanup, repair, or renaming. It does not remove, merge, or rewrite rows, and does not fix malformed CSV structure; it only identifies duplicates and reports the matching columns.
refined_descriptions.git-changelog: Generates a changelog by reading git commit history between two refs (branches, tags, or SHAs) and grouping commits into categorized entries. Unlike cron-scheduler, which converts plain-language schedules into cron expressions, this skill works only on git repository history and performs no scheduling. It does not write or validate cron expressions, schedule jobs, create or modify commits, or draft release announcements from sources other than commit history.
refined_descriptions.log-tailer: Monitors an active log file or stream and prints each new line matching a given pattern in real time. Unlike cron-scheduler, which converts plain-language schedules into cron expressions, this skill never generates or validates time-based schedules or triggers timed jobs. Does not parse archived logs, rotate files, aggregate statistics, send alerts, or fix log formats. Use only for tailing live output and filtering it as lines arrive.
refined_descriptions.api-loadtest: Sends configurable load (concurrency, request rate, duration) against a live API endpoint and reports latency percentiles, throughput, and error rates. Unlike api-mocker, it produces no mock servers or fake responses; it drives real traffic at existing endpoints to measure performance. Does not generate or parse OpenAPI specs, mock APIs, or verify functional correctness. Use for performance and load measurement of already-running APIs only.
refined_descriptions.regex-tester: Runs an existing regular expression against a list of test strings and reports each match with its capture groups. The regex must already be supplied; unlike regex-builder, it does not generate or compose regexes from plain-language descriptions. Excludes building or editing patterns, explaining regex syntax, fixing failing patterns, and running regexes against files or external tools. Use only for evaluating a given regex on provided test strings.
refined_descriptions.cron-migrator: Converts existing cron expressions between three syntaxes: standard five-field cron, Quartz (six/seven-field), and systemd timer OnCalendar values. Input an expression in one format and receive the equivalent in another, preserving timing semantics. Differs from cron-scheduler, which writes and validates expressions from plain-language schedules; this skill never generates expressions from natural-language descriptions. Excluded: creating new schedules from scratch, editing crontab or timer files, and running or managing scheduled jobs.
refined_descriptions.doc-critiquer: Reviews draft documents such as reports, articles, and essays, evaluating clarity, structure, and completeness, and returns line comments identifying problems and missing sections. Unlike email-digest, which summarizes email threads into bullet digests, this skill critiques general text drafts instead of summarizing conversations. Does not summarize documents or email threads, does not process email conversations or reply chains, does not rewrite or edit the draft, and does not generate a revised version; use email-digest for email thread summaries.
refined_descriptions.image-ocr: Extracts text from images and scanned PDFs, returning recognized words with position and bounding-box data. Reads content only and never modifies or deletes anything. Differs from pdf-redactor, which permanently removes personal data from PDFs: this skill performs no redaction, anonymization, or data removal. Does not edit images or PDFs, extract text from native (non-scanned) PDFs, or verify that sensitive data has been removed.
refined_descriptions.slide-exporter: Exports slide decks to PDF, images, or HTML handouts, with speaker notes included. Unlike pdf-redactor, which removes personal data from existing PDFs, this skill generates new output files from slide sources and never modifies or sanitizes existing PDFs. It does not redact, anonymize, or verify PDF content; it also does not edit slides or convert PDFs back into editable decks.
